name: Idaho

agency.name: Idaho Transportation Department, Division of Motor Vehicles

gaps: Plates: the engine adds two standard plates at $3.75 each; ITD's estimator also counts mailing and other plate charges that are not published as a single figure, and a buyer who keeps an existing plate pays no plate fee.

The Idaho Code page lists the age bands of the registration fee without the dollar amounts in the copy read, so the amounts ($69, $57, $45) come from the ITD registration page, and the age bands (up to 2 years old, 3 to 6, 7 and older, counted as the registration year minus the model year) from the ITD estimator.
Some Idaho resort cities levy local option sales taxes; whether they reach a vehicle sale was not stated in the Tax Commission guide read, so the engine charges the 6% state tax only.
The county registration admin fee is shown on every registration; a renewal processed by ITD online or by phone may carry a different processing fee.
No official Idaho page read for this release caps the dealer documentation fee; type the dealer's figure (the fee is taxable).

ev.label: Electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle fee

singular: Idaho taxes a car at the flat 6% state rate, collected by the county when the buyer applies for title after a private sale [istc].
A dealer documentation fee is part of the taxable price in Idaho, but a trade-in lowers it only on a dealer sale [istc].
Registration depends on age: $69 a year for a car up to two years old, $57 from three to six years and $45 after that [itd-reg].
Electric cars add $140 a year and plug-in hybrids $75, while ordinary hybrids pay nothing extra [itd-reg].
Each county adds its own admin fees, from $3 to $14 per registration and from $0 to $18.75 on top of the $14 state title fee [itd-reg].
Ada County drivers also pay the Ada County Highway District fee of $40, $36 or $24 a year depending on age, which voters decide on November 3, 2026 whether to extend beyond 2028 [achd].
Idaho no longer requires any emissions test: the Ada County program, in place since 1984, ended on June 30, 2023 [compass].
The registration fee is charged in lieu of a personal property tax on the car, so Idaho has no yearly tax on its value [minidoka].
Since July 1, 2026, Idaho stopped issuing registration stickers and no longer replaces plates every ten years [plates].

itd-reg.quote: Additional Fee – Emergency Medical Services (EMS) $1.25 Passenger Vehicle (1 or 2 years old) $69.00 Passenger Vehicle (3 or 6 years old) $57.00 Passenger Vehicle (7 or more years old) $45.00 ... Electric Vehicles Adds $140 per year ... Plug-in Hybrid Vehicles Adds $75 per year

estimator.quote: EMS and ISP Fees ($1.25 + $3.00 / year): ... New to 2 year old ... 2026 - 2024 ... Three to six years old ... 2023 - 2020 ... Seven years old ... 2019 ... HDR Fee (Ada Co. only)

achd.name: Ada County Highway District, Vehicle Registration Fee
achd.quote: Vehicles more than seven (7) years old: $24 Vehicles three (3) to seven (7) years old: $36 Vehicles one (1) and two (2) years old: $40

istc.name: Idaho State Tax Commission, Sales and Use Tax Guide for Vehicle Transactions (EPB00060)
istc.quote: Documentation fees are services the dealer agrees to provide as part of the sale. These services are included in the taxable sales price of the vehicle. ... Trade-ins aren’t allowed for private-party sales. ... He owes Idaho tax at 6%

plates.name: Idaho Transportation Department, License plates
plates.quote: As of July 1, 2026, the DMV will stop providing registration stickers and license plates will no longer be replaced every ten years. ... Standard plates cost $3.75 per plate.

compass.name: Air Quality Board (COMPASS), Last Day for Emissions Testing in Ada County
compass.quote: Today, June 30, 2023, marks the last day of Ada County’s emissions testing program, in place since 1984. The program will officially end at midnight tonight.

minidoka.name: Minidoka County Assessor, Motor Vehicle Licenses
minidoka.quote: The operating fee for motor vehicles in Idaho is in lieu of personal property taxes (§49-401, I.C.).
